hypothesis: The parent bumped CTS sink-cluster diameter/size, which made the clock tree worse. Revert that and instead disable CTS sink clustering entirely (cluster_size 1 / diameter small) so CTS builds a balanced H-tree with per-sink buffering; this reduces long clock detours and buffer-induced congestion, lowering propagated-clock WNS/TNS without increasing overflow.
analysis: Mixed: hypothesis only partly holds. Ariane133-ng45 improves TNS (-8.8%) but WNS worsens (+6.8%), and bp_fe-ng45 WNS degrades (+7.0%) despite TNS gain—suggesting disabling clustering helps some sinks but hurts critical paths, plausibly from added per-sink buffering/detour on tight paths. bp-ng45 improves both. Robust score is negative (-0.019), so the change is not a clear win. Next step: apply clustering disable selectively (e.g., only non-critical sink groups or cap cluster diameter) and re-run to isolate the WNS regression on ariane/bp_fe.
